chapter: Long Island years and Battle's estate
title: Battle's recording equipment
summary: Before he died Battle bought expensive recording gear, which was moved to a friend's basement.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Got a good sound on Eddie Banfield.
That's when he moved out of his studios. But just before he died, he had bought some fabulous equipment. I went down and he got recording machines like this, cost him $1500 second-hand.
Yeah, well, I mean, you know, you can pay that, you know, for your --
And he got, I mean, real things. So we took them away and let John Smith take them in his basement
and he give a receipt to me for the estate to keep them because somebody would take them. I was with him when he went and bought . Who's Charlie Smith?

Was a guitar player that was with (inaudible) -- John Smith, played banjo. He was a good (inaudible) and he died, too. So, he's got a lot of the things now. Took . He's got a 15 or 20 mikes, you know, and two of them I opened up and they cost $100 apiece. I don't know what they were for. Big gold mikes. Paid $100 a mike. Now, if ever he's going to use them, I don't know. But we got all that stuff. (Inaudible).
Yes, inside out. That was the trouble with that.
No, no. It was loaded on the tape inside out. That's why it didn't record.
